economy.summary: In her March 2026 campaign announcement she said she wants families to be able to find good-paying jobs in the region, citing her work to bring investments that improve infrastructure, expand housing, and boost the manufacturing sector.
economy.short: Cites work bringing investments for infrastructure, housing, manufacturing jobs.

taxes.summary: Voted in May 2024 for Senate Bill 269, which would cut the state personal income tax rate from 3.07% to 2.8% and eliminate the gross receipts tax on electricity bills; she called it the largest tax cut for working families in Pennsylvania history.
taxes.short: Voted to cut income tax; called it historic family relief.

abortion.summary: Voted in July 2022 for Senate Bill 106, a proposed state constitutional amendment stating the constitution does not grant a right to abortion; she earlier voted for a 2017 bill banning abortion after 20 weeks and a 2019 bill prohibiting abortions sought because of a Down syndrome diagnosis.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating no constitutional right to abortion.

healthcare.summary: Chairs the Senate Health and Human Services Committee; her March 2026 campaign announcement says she supports expanding access to quality health care in the region and advocating for first responders and emergency services.
healthcare.short: Supports expanding health care access; chairs Senate health committee.

energy.summary: In a January 2022 letter to the editor she opposed Pennsylvania joining the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative without legislative approval, calling the program a tax that would be passed on to electricity consumers and saying it would make Pennsylvania less competitive and less energy-diverse.
energy.short: Opposes joining RGGI carbon compact; calls it consumer tax.

guns.summary: Co-sponsored Senate Bill 565 of 2021, which would have allowed carrying a concealed firearm without a license; the Senate passed the bill 29-21 in November 2021 and it did not become law.
guns.short: Co-sponsored bill allowing concealed carry without a license.

economy.summary: After securing the Democratic nomination through a primary write-in campaign in 2026, she said her priorities include strengthening local businesses and ensuring that Harrisburg works for the people, not special interests.
economy.short: Says priorities include strengthening local businesses.

taxes.summary: After securing the Democratic nomination through a primary write-in campaign in 2026, she said her priorities include low taxes.
taxes.short: Says her priorities include low taxes.

education.summary: After securing the Democratic nomination through a primary write-in campaign in 2026, she said her priorities include supporting public education; she works as a school nurse.
education.short: Says priorities include supporting public education.

healthcare.summary: A registered nurse, she said after securing the Democratic nomination through a primary write-in campaign in 2026 that her priorities include protecting rural healthcare.
healthcare.short: Says priorities include protecting rural healthcare.
